Title: [LSJ] Third Tradition vs Create Gargoyle wording.

Messages.Author: www.h...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Hi!

Just wanted to check something that came up during a game a few nights
ago.
The Third Tradition: Progeny (along with Trophy: Progeny and Creation
Rites) says that you may search your "library (shuffle afterward), ash
heap OR hand" (my emphasis) while Create Gargoyle uses the wording
"hand, library AND ash heap" (my emphasis again).

Is there any difference between those two?

It might not matter that often but in case someone who played a Third
Tradition: Progeny started with searching xer library and didn't find
any discipline card, would xe be allowed to take one from xer hand or
ash heap afterwards?
With the current card text it's a bit unclear to us, since the "or"
could mean that you have to chose before searching.

Create Gargoyle
Type: Action
Requires: non-sterile Tremere/Tremere antitribu
Cost: 2 pool
+1 stealth action. Requires a non-sterile vampire.
Put this card into play. This card represents a 2-capacity, non-
unique, slave Gargoyle (enslaved to the acting vampire's clan) with
basic Visceratika [vis] and flight [FLIGHT]. You may go through your
hand, library and ash heap to find a master: Discipline card and place
it on this Gargoyle. Move up to 3 blood from the acting vampire to
this Gargoyle. This Gargoyle is the same sect as the acting vampire.
This Gargoyle cannot act this turn.

Third Tradition: Progeny
Type: Action
Requires: prince,justicar,non-sterile
Cost: 1 blood
+1 stealth action. Requires a ready non-Sterile prince or justicar.
Put this card in play; it becomes a non-unique 1-capacity vampire of
the same clan as the acting vampire. You may go through your library
(shuffle afterward), ash heap or hand to find a Discipline card for
this vampire. Move up to 2 blood from the acting vampire to this
vampire. This vampire cannot take any actions this turn.

Messages.Author: Baaliprimogen
Messages.Body:


I don't know if there is. If there is my only guess would be that with
the gargoyle card, you may search everything and find the card you
want. But with the progeny you have to choose. If you choose your
library, but you don't have any masters there, then it's too late to
take from Ashheap.

Messages.Body:

>want. But with the progeny you have to choose. If you choose your
>library, but you don't have any masters there, then it's too late to
>take from Ashheap.

However, because the ash heap is a matter of public record and you can
always look at your own hand, you could look through both of those
anyway, without any enabling text. Since you should know how many
discipline cards there are in your deck for a deck using breeders, you'd
then know what's where.

> However, because the ash heap is a matter of public record and you can
> always look at your own hand, you could look through both of those
> anyway, without any enabling text.  Since you should know how many
> discipline cards there are in your deck for a deck using breeders, you'd
> then know what's where.

Yeah, I know that you can look through your hand and ash heap before
playing the card/s (or after succeeding with the action but before
searching through your library, I suppose). But the question still
stands about whether the wording on Create Gargoyle and Third
Tradition: Progeny is intentionally different (regarding the
searching) or if it's just a "mishap".
We can pretend that someone forgot if xe put 6 or 7 discipline masters
in the deck since stuff like that happens sometimes, especially during
casual games when trying new decks. After playing a Third Tradition:
Progeny, would it be legal for xem to go through the library first,
and afterwards pick a discipline card from xer ash heap?

We've always played as if the cards had said "and", without really
thinking more about it. But as it came up during a game I thought I'd
might as well get it checked.
